correctness.rationale: The prime number theorem supplies the required disjoint prime pairs; the Chinese remainder theorem yields an infinite residue class of \(k\). For each pair the constructed \(u_i\) is even, \(v_i\) is odd, and \(u_iv_i=n(n+1)/2\), yielding integral endpoints \(a_i,b_i\) satisfying \(2\le a_i\le b_i\le n-1\) and exact half-total sum. The distinct lengths \(u_i<n/2\) and their complements of length above \(n/2\) give \(2h\) arcs. The progression modulo \(4P\) has positive density. Quantitative PNT supplies primes at scale \(X=h(\log h)^2\), so \(\log n_h\le(2+o(1))h\log h\), proving the limsup coefficient at least \(1\). The executable verifies examples and finite direct counts, not the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Half-total is the complement-invariant center of the arc-sum problem. The construction proves arbitrarily large representation multiplicity along full positive-density congruence classes even as global completeness fails, and extracts a quantitative lower bound for extremal central multiplicity. The constrained arc and positive-density requirements make it more than generic odd-divisor recomputation; future distribution and upper-bound questions directly concern this precise invariant.
